diveTitle: What actually happens when you convert to PDF
diveSubtitle: How animations, fonts and notes carry over.
dive1Title: Animations and transitions — what happens to them
dive1Desc: A PDF is a static document, so animations and slide transitions don't carry over — each slide converts to its final, fully-revealed state, as if every animation had already played. If a slide relies on a build sequence to make sense, review it after conversion.
dive2Desc: By default, the PDF contains only what's visible on the slide itself, not your speaker notes underneath. If you need notes included, most presentation software has a specific \"print with notes\" layout option to select before exporting or printing to PDF.
dive3Desc: Video and audio files embedded in a slide can't play inside a PDF, since PDF isn't a media format. They convert to a static preview image, a thumbnail frame of the video, rather than a playable clip.
dive4Desc: Whatever aspect ratio your presentation uses, whether 4:3, 16:9, or a custom size, the PDF pages match it exactly. Each page is sized to one slide, so widescreen presentations produce widescreen-shaped PDF pages, not standard portrait pages with slides shrunk to fit.
dive5Title: Fonts not installed on our servers
dive5Desc: If your presentation uses a font that isn't embedded in the file and isn't available on our conversion servers, it's substituted with the closest match, which can shift text positioning slightly. Embedding fonts in your presentation before converting avoids this entirely.
dive6Desc: Each slide becomes exactly one PDF page, in the order they appear in your presentation. There's no option to combine multiple slides per page, like a handout layout, with this converter — that's a distinct layout you'd set up in the presentation software's own export settings.
faqSubtitle: Everything you might want to know before hitting convert.
faq1Question: Is this PPT to PDF converter free?
faq1Answer: Yes, it is free to start. No credit card or trial is needed.
faq2Question: Will my slides look the same in the PDF?
faq2Answer: In most cases, yes. Layouts, images, and text formatting are preserved faithfully. Slide animations and transitions won't carry over (since PDFs are static), but the visual content of each slide will look as expected.
faq3Question: What happens to my files after conversion?
faq3Answer: Your files are deleted from our servers within 1 hour. We process everything over encrypted connections and do not view or share your presentations.
faq4Question: Can I convert multiple PowerPoint files at once?
faq4Answer: On the free plan you convert one file at a time, up to 5 MB. Starter unlocks batch uploads — up to 10 files at once, each up to 20 MB — converted to individual PDFs you can download separately or as a zip.
faq5Question: What if my PDF looks different from the original?
faq5Answer: Slight differences can happen if your presentation uses custom fonts not embedded in the file, or certain advanced effects. For best results, embed your fonts before exporting from PowerPoint.
faq6Question: Can I open the converted PDF on my phone or tablet?
faq6Answer: Yes. The output is a standard PDF file that opens in any PDF reader — Adobe Acrobat, your browser, Apple Books, Google Drive, and so on.
